analysis: This documentation-only change adds docs/architecture/inference.md head lines 595-611, a paragraph on the Gated DeltaNet prefill kernels. Each process probes the packed and then the rows kernel for each instantiation (dtype and head geometry) on a fixed probe window. It keeps the first kernel that bit-matches gated_delta_step, or falls back to the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than minT=16 always use the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can force a kernel for A/B measurement. The text claims that bit-exactness keeps checkpoint-capture state consistent, which bears on prefix-cache correctness (T-041 cache bindings) and on output integrity (T-007/T-027). This is a performance and correctness claim. It does not change scoping, encryption, TTL or authorization. The prefix-cache cacheSalt scoping described in T-041 is unaffected by kernel selection. One residual question is outside the supplied evidence: whether forcing packed or rows through the env var bypasses the bit-exact probe. If it does, recurrent state could diverge across chunks and corrupt a restored checkpoint. That would be an availability or integrity issue for the operator's own provider (an ADV-001 operator can already manipulate outputs, T-007), not a cross-tenant leak. The GatedDelta.swift source was not supplied, so this needs code review. The remaining text in both units (Nemotron Super and GLM sections) is unchanged context according to the complete range map. It describes tenant-scoped prefix reuse (lines 232-238 and 522-524), which is consistent with T-041. No regression was identified.
